fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Street Frontage; Open Terrain; Scattered Vegetation Near Structure; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Vegetation Near Access Route; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the street.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflectors on both sides to define the entry point for responding units arriving at speed.
• Keep the full width of the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so emergency vehicles can reach the structure without stopping.
• Trim any vegetation along the driveway edges that narrows the travel width or blocks driver sightlines.
• Create a dedicated turnaround area near the structure large enough for a fire or rescue vehicle to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Mark the turnaround area clearly so arriving crews can identify it immediately on approach.
• Keep scattered vegetation near the structure trimmed back so it does not block walking paths around the building or access to exterior doors and utility shutoffs.
• Maintain a clear path from the driveway to each exterior door so crews on foot can move directly to entry points without navigating around plantings or obstacles.
• Keep the landscaped area immediately around the structure free of tall, dense, or overhanging plantings that would slow crew movement or block visibility of the structure from the driveway.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Long Driveway; Grass Cover; Brush Area; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster closest to the structure to open up space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Trim low-hanging branches on trees near the structure so branches do not extend close to the roofline or walls.
• Cut and remove brush in the brush area nearest to the structure.
• Mow or cut grass surrounding the structure, particularly during dry periods when grass is brown or dry.
• Thin scattered shrubs within the mixed vegetation area closest to the structure to break up continuous plant coverage near the building.
• Keep the long driveway clear of overhanging branches along its full length to allow emergency vehicle access.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of brush and overgrown vegetation along both sides that could close in over the travel lane.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the main road, particularly for emergency responders using the single access route.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structure by preventing shrubs and grass from re-establishing in those cleared zones.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from within the mixed vegetation area directly surrounding the structure.
• Separate any wood piles, outdoor furniture, or stored materials from shrubs and vegetation growing nearby.
